bull_bear.body:
- **Underleveraged**; healthy debt-equity. Finance cost ~INR 30 cr FY26 (mostly working-capital driven; INR 2–2.2 cr one-off refinancing/processing charge). Refinancing underway at both Refex Industries and Venwind for lower borrowing cost. **No immediate fundraise** (promoter warrants deliberately not subscribed). **Demerger** of mobility to unlock value (different investor set for EV/sustainable vs core).
- **Promoter pledge:** ~**41%** (rose vs guidance to reduce). Mgmt: removal tied to loan closure (contractual); monthly payments ongoing; expects **partial/large-part removal over next ~6 months**.
bull_bear.title: Capital Allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Working-capital intensity:** Receivable days ~105–130 (mgmt guides 105–125 days steady); contract assets/unbilled ~INR 700+ cr — execution-to-cash lag a structural drag.
- **Diversification execution:** Three very different businesses (logistics services, heavy WTG manufacturing, EV mobility) — execution & capital-allocation complexity.
- **Promoter pledge at 41%** rose despite prior reduction guidance — credibility/overhang risk.
- **Diesel cost** only partially passed through (40–60%).
- **IT search / enforcement overhang** (raised by analyst) — mgmt says all disclosures done, no expected financial/reputational impact; one caller praised regaining "industrial confidence" post regulator/enforcement issues.
- **Wind order-pipeline guidance soft** — only INR 1,860 cr firm; further orders not yet signed.
- **Demerger timeline** subject to NCLT court process (~75–90 days, ~August 2026 expected); company-side compliances 100% done.
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: Confident, measured, repeatedly **refused to give numeric guidance** ("we'll have a good growth," "not speaking on any number"). Emphasis on **quality of profit/margin over revenue**, governance, and asset-light scaling. CMD Anil Jain notably "relaxed" vs prior calls (deliberately delegating Q&A to build leaders). Strong analyst sentiment / praise for management.
bull_bear.title: Management Tone

bull_bear.body:
- Revenue "degrowth" is **deliberate de-risking** (exiting INR 220 cr low-margin trading), not demand loss — core ash grew 28%.
- Coal vs ash revenue split is **structurally impossible** due to reverse-logistics fleet optimization.
- Wind receivables are **LC-backed** → cleaner cash cycle than the working-capital-heavy ash business.
- "11–12%" prior guidance was **PAT margin**, not EBITDA — a recurring analyst misunderstanding.
- Imported-coal substitution does NOT hurt ash business (domestic coal ~3x ash content).
- Coal gasification (govt syn-gas program) is unrelated to thermal/ash demand.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious Points

bull_bear.body:
- "Net debt free balance sheet, providing greater financial flexibility to support its future growth plans", alongside "Strong internal cash generation from contract-led businesses".
- "FY26 ROCE stands at ~22.0%, with further upside potential"; the historical chart shows ROCE of 18% (Mar-25), 17% (Sep-25) and 22% (Mar-26), and ROE of 15% (Mar-25), 13% (Sep-25) and 16% (Mar-26).
- Debt to equity shown at 0.08 (Mar-25), 0.08 (Sep-25) and 0.10 (Mar-26).
- "Strengthening dividend track record over recent years" and "Value creation through stock split (1:5 ratio) in FY24"; the split-adjusted total dividend per share series is shown against FY21/FY23/FY24/FY26 as 0.3 / 0.4 / 0.1 / 1.5, with the FY26 dividend subject to shareholders' approval.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Coal & Ash Handling (CORE):** India's largest organized player; integrated ash logistics + material handling + environmental-compliance. Coal-in / ash-out **reverse logistics** (rail "rack" mode or road) maximizes fleet utilization — hence coal vs ash revenue **cannot be split**. Escalation clauses cover **40–60%** of diesel cost (rest is a cost hit). TAM cited **~INR 75,000 cr**; Refex at ~INR 2,000 cr ≈ **3% share**. Nearest competitor estimated at ~25% of Refex's size; rest fragmented (1–5 plants each), none listed.
- **Wind / WTG (Venwind Refex Power):** German-licensed **5.3 MW turbine** platform; **ALMM approval received** in FY26 (key milestone); deliveries commenced Feb-2026, phased dispatch. Receivables backed by **LC** (short cycle, separate from standalone). EBITDA margin ~8% currently.
- **EV / Mobility (Refex Green Mobility):** Crossed **INR 100 cr revenue** in 3 years of operation; shifting to **asset-light** model with clean-fuel + enterprise-led scaling; progressing toward profitability. Being **demerged** (see below). Tailwind: PM's push to shift govt/agency fleets to EVs.
- **Refrigerant gases & Power trading:** Both **discontinued/exited** — refrigerant stock liquidated, residual receivable to close; power trading fully out.
business.title: Segment Detail

business.body:
- ⭐ **Refex itself** — primary beneficiary of structural thermal-power growth (50 GW new capacity), tightening ash/environmental-compliance norms, and India's largest organized ash-logistics moat (40 plants, proprietary logistics tech).
- ✅ Govt EV-shift policy → tailwind for the (to-be-demerged) **Refex Green Mobility**.
- ✅ Domestic wind capacity-addition / IPP push → tailwind for **Venwind** (ALMM-approved 5.3 MW platform).
- (Fragmented unorganized ash players remain the displaced incumbents.)

---
business.title: Challenges → Beneficiaries

business.body:
- Three business verticals under Refex Industries Limited: "Wind – Global tech powered wind turbine manufacturing", "Ash – Sustainable utilization of ash" and "Premium Corporate Mobility – Tech-led mobility solutions"; 23+ years of experience, presence across 14+ states, 500+ consolidated team size.
- Ash & coal handling described as "Largest Organized Player in India" — established 2018, 40+ plants serviced and 50+ million MT of ash utilized in 8 years, with clients including NTPCs & JVs, state GENCOs (MP, TN, AP), Damodar Valley Corp and Adani Power.
- Moat framed as an "execution-intensive model enabled by deep expertise, integration, and technology", end-to-end integrated ash management across evacuation, transport, utilization and compliance, and "formalizing a fragmented and unorganized ecosystem through structured service delivery".
- Venwind Refex Power Limited claims to be the "First company in India to receive ALMM certification for a 5.3 MW wind turbine", with ALMM listing for the 5.3 MW GWH turbine completed.
- Regulatory moat in ash: MoEF & CC notification (31.12.2021) and amendment (30.12.2022) mandate 100% ash utilization for thermal power plants, with non-compliance penalties of ₹1,000 per ton and a 10-year legacy-ash roadmap (20% year 1, 35% year 2, 50% years 3-10 annually).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Demerger] RGML merges into RIL and RGML's shares held by RIL are cancelled; the mobility undertaking is then carved out of RIL into a new company, Refex Mobility Limited (RML), which will issue shares to all RIL shareholders at a 1:1 swap ratio and be listed as an independent entity — the stated rationale being "focused growth, value unlocking, and independent balance sheets across two differentiated business platforms".
- [Demerger status] BSE, NSE and lender approvals received; NCLT approval received for convening stakeholder meetings, with the Equity Shareholders' Meeting scheduled for 5 August 2026 and all scheme-related notices issued.
- [Regulation] MoEF & CC initial-cycle compliance deadlines vary by current utilization — 3 years if >80%, 4 years if 60-80%, 5 years if <60% — with mandatory cleanup of accumulated ash stocks effective from 1 April 2022.
- [Policy tailwind — wind] India's installed wind capacity ~50 GW (as of March 2025), 4th globally; MNRE wind capacity target of 140-150 GW by 2030; 500 GW non-fossil fuel capacity target; domestic manufacturing capacity 18+ GW p.a.; GST on wind equipment reduced from 12% to 5%; updated national climate targets set 60% non-fossil installed power capacity by 2035.
- [Ownership] Promoter & Promoter Group holding rose from 53.33% (Sep-25) to 56.56% (Jun-26); FIIs 0.93%, DIIs 0.38%, Public & Others 42.13% as on 30 June 2026; 137,219,448 outstanding shares.
- [History] Refex Refrigerants Private Limited commenced operations in the refrigerant gas sector in 2002, listed on BSE in 2007, set up a 5 MW solar plant in Rajasthan (2012), renamed Refex Industries Limited (2018), commenced ash and coal handling for thermal power plants, launched RGML mobility operations in Chennai in Sep'23 and incorporated Venwind Refex Power Limited (2024).
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: - Margin re-rate driven by **mix shift** (trading out, service in) — mgmt insists service margins were "always good." FY26: COGS −18% vs revenue −10%; manpower cost reduced via technology/automation. Diesel inflation only **40–60% pass-through**. Sustainable blended EBITDA **15–18%**; Q4 20.1% defended as sustainable.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & Cost

latest_quarter.body: - **Q4 FY26 (this call):** Std rev INR 701 cr (+18% YoY), EBITDA INR 141 cr (20.1%), PAT INR 94 cr (+67%). FY26: rev INR 2,039 cr (−10%, trading-exit driven), EBITDA INR 350 cr (17.2%, +68%), PAT INR 247 cr. Wind execution began (INR 238 cr); ALMM approval received. Refrigerant gas + power trading fully exited. Mobility demerger at NCLT (~Aug-2026 expected). Ash order pipeline INR 1,500 cr; Wind order book INR 1,860 cr (INR 1,500 cr open). Promoter pledge 41% (rose). Daily ash handling 68–70k tons/day, target 90–95k.
latest_quarter.title: QoQ Log

outlook.body:
- **Coal & Ash Handling:** Same growth in FY27 as FY26 (i.e. **double-digit %** core growth); order pipeline **~INR 1,500 cr**. No capacity constraint — ramp is gradual, location-by-location.
- **Daily handling volume:** Currently **68,000–70,000 tons/day**; targeting ramp to **90,000–95,000 tons/day** (clarified this is a *future-year* target, achievable within current FY27, gradual).
- **Wind (Venwind):** Order book **INR 1,860 cr**; **INR 238 cr executed** in FY26 (Q4); **~INR 1,500 cr balance to be executed in FY27** → wind revenue could be **INR 1,700–1,800 cr** in FY27 (per analyst math, mgmt confirmed all old orders complete this year + possible new orders). "Massive growth" YoY on consol basis. Capacity target **~2 GW by next year-end**.
- **Margins:** Blended EBITDA margin guided **15–18%** sustainable (Q4's 20.1% described as sustainable, supported by service mix). Wind current EBITDA margin **~8%**, expected to *improve via localization* and to stay better than competitors. CFO: focus is to **maintain** current EBITDA margin given geopolitical uncertainty.
- **Net-profit guidance note:** Earlier "11–12%" guidance was on **PAT/net profit**, NOT EBITDA (clarification to analyst).
- **Capex/fundraise:** No immediate fundraise required for Refex Industries; sufficient internal accruals + bank limits.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL)

outlook.body:
- **Coal & Ash:** ~INR 1,500 cr order pipeline; includes long-term contracts e.g. **APGENCO 3-year contract** (kicks in at start of FY); fresh orders ~INR 120–130 cr added in Q4. Operating across **40 thermal power plants** across India.
- **Wind (Venwind):** **INR 1,860 cr** firm order book; INR 238 cr executed; **~INR 1,500 cr open** for FY27. "Advanced stage" negotiations on a few more orders (not yet disclosable — earlier media chatter of ~INR 2,000 cr further pipeline NOT confirmed as firm).
outlook.title: Order Book / Pipeline

outlook.body:
- **Thermal-power structural tailwind:** ~**50 GW** new thermal capacity to be added in India over next 4–5 years; India coal consumption ~800 mn tons rising YoY. **Domestic coal ash content 37–40%** (vs imported 12–13%) → ash handling demand resilient regardless of coal imports. Coal gasification (syn-gas) program is **separate** and does NOT impact thermal/ash business.
- **Wind sector:** Structurally attractive — rising capacity-addition targets, stronger IPP participation, localization initiatives, improving policy visibility. Localization of components is the next 1–2 year margin lever.
- **EV mobility:** Optionality via demerger value-unlock + govt EV-shift policy.
- **Reclassification optionality:** Application filed (~2 months prior) to move out of "industrial gases" exchange classification → better peer comparability.
outlook.title: Growth / Optionality

deepdive.thesis: Refex has structurally re-shaped from a low-margin **trading** house (refrigerant gases + power trading, both now exited) into a **service/logistics-led** business anchored by India's largest **coal & ash handling** franchise, with **wind WTG (Venwind)** entering active execution and the **EV/mobility** arm being demerged — driving a sharp margin re-rate (FY26 EBITDA margin 17.2% vs 9.2% prior) despite headline revenue degrowth.

risks.note: Ash & Coal Handling continued to be the Company's principal business segment; the business model depends on ongoing thermal power generation, ash-utilisation regulation, and relationships with a relatively concentrated set of large power producers (IPPs/CPPs, NTPC, state GENCOs).
risks.risk: Concentration in Ash & Coal Handling, which remains dependent on continued coal-based thermal power generation

risks.note: The Company discontinued its Power Trading & Refrigerant business during the year (relatively low-margin), which changed the revenue base and reflects a history of active portfolio restructuring that could recur.
risks.risk: Recent discontinuation of the Power Trading and Refrigerant Gas businesses

risks.note: Venwind Refex Power Limited only commenced revenue contribution in FY26 (its first full year of active execution), and its growth depends on converting a confirmed order book of over 400 MW into executed, revenue-generating projects.

The ash management business depends on an execution platform of over 2,500 owned and leased vehicles capable of handling more than 70,000 MT of ash per day; disruptions to fleet availability, logistics, or utilisation could affect service delivery.
risks.risk: Asset- and fleet-intensive ash-handling execution platform

risks.note: The proposed demerger of the mobility business (into a separately listed Refex Mobility Limited) had achieved approvals from stock exchanges and lenders during the year but remained subject to further regulatory/shareholder approvals and implementation risk.
risks.risk: Execution risk on the proposed mobility demerger

risks.note: The mobility business (RGML) serves a diversified but still developing customer base of multinational corporations and large domestic enterprises across five metro markets (Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Delhi NCR); loss of large corporate clients or slower formalisation of the corporate mobility market could affect growth.
risks.risk: New-vertical customer concentration in Premium Corporate Mobility
